acceptance.criterion_verbatim: a registry section recording what is in there, keyed so a consumer can look a document class up and reach it.
acceptance.invocation: Read of the deliverable sections 3 and 11 (capability registry) and section 9 (per-class read matrix).
acceptance.output_evidence: Section 11 keys on CAPABILITY -> tool -> exercised state. Section 9 keys on DOCUMENT CLASS -> tool -> exercised result -> readable?, so a consumer looks up their class and learns both which call to make and what they will actually get back: .xlsx -> read_site_workbook -> FULL cell text; text/csv/md -> read_site_file -> text; .pdf/.docx/.pptx -> read_document -> RENDITION ONLY, NO TEXT; any -> profile_site_file -> bytes + sha256, server-side. The readable? column is the load-bearing one: it is what distinguishes a REACHABLE class from a READABLE one.
acceptance.denominator: 8 read-side capabilities registered (7 exercised, 1 deferred); 4 document classes keyed; 2 write tools registered as OUT OF SCOPE.

acceptance.invocation: Read of sections 6 (why search is deferred), 7 (unverified premises table), 11 (capability table marking the unexercised member), 12 (declared bound + scope-of-every-absence-claim table).
acceptance.output_evidence: Five premises tabulated with status: (1) the 15-site list is FALSE AS STATED as a tenant set -- it is Andrew's VISIBLE set and a FLOOR; (2) one-library-per-site UNVERIFIED beyond 3 of 15; (3) the wildcard as an enumeration primitive UNVERIFIED -- it is a query; (4) unexercised tools NOT CLAIMED; (5) no-quota-on-this-surface UNKNOWN, not established, because absence of a published limit is not absence of a limit. acceptance.criterion_verbatim: a DENOMINATOR on the document universe, or a DECLARED BOUND stating why it cannot be closed. An absence verdict NAMES THE SCOPE IT SEARCHED (site/drive/library) -- the firm-partition lesson generalises to any partitioned store, and a 404 in the wrong library is the wrong question asked cleanly.
acceptance.output_evidence: DECLARED BOUND in place of a denominator, with the reason: the universe cannot be closed by this method because (a) the site set is a floor scoped to one identity's visibility, and (b) closing a document count needs a recursive walk, which is the harvest the call-shape rule forbids -- and the listing metadata already carries the bound without it. Bounded instead: Shared root = 78 folders + ~15 root files, each folder carrying childCount and size (Marketing 3.2GB, Software 3.0GB, Systematic Equity 2.4GB, Research 1.5GB, OCIO Models 1.6GB). EVERY ABSENCE CLAIM NAMES ITS SCOPE in a dedicated table: document classes -> Shared DEFAULT LIBRARY, ROOT LEVEL ONLY, plus 3 folders of 49Financial; library count -> 3 of 15 sites, default library only; site set -> queries, a floor, Andrew's visible set and never the tenant's.
acceptance.denominator: A declared bound replaces the denominator, with its reason; 3 absence-shaped claims, 3 carrying their searched scope.

mutant.description: Sufficiency mutant on the DEFAULT-LIBRARY limitation: the tools reach only a site's default library, so if any probed site carried a second library the registry's file-listing claims would be silently short. Probed three sites to try to find one.
mutant.expected: If multi-library sites exist in the probed set, list_site_drives returns more than one documentLibrary for at least one.
mutant.observed: DID NOT FIRE on the probed set -- 49Financial, Shared and OpalOCIO each returned exactly ONE documentLibrary, so default-library-only costs nothing THERE. Reported honestly as REAL IN THE TOOL and UNEXERCISED ON WHAT WAS TESTED, with 12 of 15 sites untested and the failure mode named: a multi-library site is under-read with NO signal. A non-firing mutant is reported as non-firing, never as absence of the hazard.

determinism.method: Drive probes and site listings re-run against the same three sites.
determinism.observed: Identical: one documentLibrary each, same drive ids, same webUrls, same listing metadata.

declared_exclusions.reason: Structurally unobtainable by this method, and the criterion permits a DECLARED BOUND instead. Closing it would need a recursive walk (forbidden by the call-shape rule) over a site set that is itself only a floor.
The list_site_files / read_site_* tools reach the DEFAULT library only. Untested on 12 of 15 sites.

declared_exclusions.item: Any claim about the TENANT rather than Andrew's visible set
declared_exclusions.reason: The gateway is OAuth'd as a named human; an inaccessible site does not error, it simply does not appear in the result.

surprises: The one-character-twin hazard has a SharePoint analogue: the Opal site query and the wildcard query differ by 9 sites with no error, and the missed set contains the largest corpus on the tenant.
A pre-existing over-grant surfaced incidentally in the same session: auth/ credential code held lane ANY under .tools/**, and the integrations/** grant narrowed it to ANY_EXEC_OR_AE.
